mentl/a68308a:
Closes named peer #94. Substrate:

1. WatBuffer effect with wat_collect() op — buffer extraction from a
   scoped wat_emit accumulator.

2. wat_to_string handler — intercepts BOTH WasmOut.wat_emit AND
   WatBuffer.wat_collect, accumulating bytes into a `buf` state, returning
   the buffer on wat_collect. One handler, two effects. Per
   protocol_handler_is_state_is_closure_is_evidence.md: the buffer IS
   the state IS the closure IS the evidence.

3. collect_fn_emit_records — deep-walk projects every fn-bearing variant
   (LMakeClosure / LMakeContinuation / LDeclareFn) to a (name, params,
   body, captures_count) tuple. Tree-traversal order matches the prior
   emit_fns_expr order byte-for-byte so $<name>_idx globals still align.

4. emit_one_fn_to_string — installs wat_to_string locally; emit_fn_body's
   perform wat_emit goes to the buffer; wat_collect returns the buffer.
   Each branch of parallel_map gets its own handler instance.

5. emit_functions — page-topology:
     lowered
       |> collect_fn_emit_records
       |> parallel_map(emit_one_fn_to_string)
       |> for_each((s) => perform wat_emit(s))

   Per-fn emit dispatches across cores; sequential output preserves
   source order (Q-B.7.3 determinism).

emit_fns_list + emit_fns_expr deleted (the recursive emit-in-place walk
was the foreign-fluency form when parallel_map + wat_to_string substrate
was missing). Both are present now; the collect + parallel + sequential-
output pattern IS the cargo-class per-fn emit substrate.

turbosort/a654052:
The publish and release steps each ended in || echo, so a bad registry
token, a broken package, or a failed gh call still exited 0 and the tag
looked shipped while nothing reached crates.io. Replace both with honest
idempotency: skip the upload only when the exact version is already on
crates.io, skip release creation only when the release already exists,
and let every other failure fail the job. Also refuse to publish when
the pushed tag disagrees with the Cargo.toml version, and pass --locked
so the publish builds against the committed lockfile like CI does.
